# FLEA cleanup and runtime-power exclusion

Owner: [#689](https://github.com/ahnhy1324/crystalhd/issues/689).
This is a maintained-driver prerequisite for a later opt-in experiment,
not enabled clock gating or a temperature/endurance result. Runtime
`FleaEnablePWM=false`, the installed official 1.3 runtime and firmware remain
unchanged.

## Problem and change

The completed [#376 investigation](https://github.com/ahnhy1324/crystalhd/issues/376)
included an experimental asleep-cleanup guard in source `e38a2f803250`.
Current maintained source already includes checked physical transitions,
fault retention and owner/FLL fences, but lacked that cleanup admission guard.
Copying the old point-in-time check would still leave a race: after it releases
`hw->lock`, IRQ-tail `CMD_COMP` can enter low power before cleanup stops engines
or retires resources.

The maintained fix uses a nested cleanup hold protected by the same hardware
lock as runtime-PM reservations. It covers context retirement, TX cancellation,
RX stop and FLEA device stop. While held, completion-driven PM, FLL publication
and the final power-state setter return busy. Device-stop state publication
remains possible without dropping the outer retirement hold. The last hold is
released before the context is freed, and releasing it does not initiate PM.

| State at cleanup admission | Required behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Non-FLEA | Preserve the existing backend path. |
| FLEA already faulted | Reject and preserve the retained resources. |
| Transition already reserved | Return busy; do not misclassify a temporary snapshot during wake as a new terminal fault. |
| `LP_COMPLETE` or saved power snapshot | Publish the existing terminal fault and retain resources, including when the PWM flag is off. Do not reset or attempt another wake. |
| Clocked `ACTIVE` or `LP_PENDING`, no snapshot | Acquire a cleanup hold when PWM is enabled; preserve the ordinary disabled path. A failed FLL publication after physical wake is not itself an uncertain physical wake. |
| Initial/stopped context, no snapshot | Preserve normal initialization/shutdown cleanup. |
| Globally serialized terminal PCI removal | Existing checked MASTER-off/drain/IRQ-retirement proof remains authoritative. A successful proof can free retained backing; failed proof quarantines it. This memory-only path does not need to pass ordinary asleep cleanup. |

The hold excludes runtime power changes, not concurrent cleanup callers. All
existing process, queue, firmware-command and IRQ serialization is still
required; the [DMA contract](../../../DMA.md) describes the resource boundary.

## Verification scope

Production helper bodies and the four real cleanup callers are exercised by
the existing source-extraction suites. Tests retain their scripted device/PCI
leaves; this is device-free evidence, not a physical quiescence or recovery
measurement. The shared extractor [flea-cleanup.awk](../../flea-cleanup.awk)
selects original helper bodies, not a replacement cleanup implementation.

The checks cover nested holds across callbacks, IRQ completion between the
admission check and cleanup, final-setter refusal, success/failure release,
retained TX/RX/context ownership and terminal proof failure/success. Existing
PLL/CKE/readback failure and post-wake FLL-retry controls remain intact.
Synthetic asleep fixtures must explicitly expect refused normal cleanup;
ordinary fixtures must still require successful ordinary cleanup.

Executed on 2026-11-26 against maintained base `1427d2de0825` plus this change:

| Check | Actual result |
| --- | --- |
| `make flea-power-check` | PASS in normal/ASan+UBSan builds, watchdog off/on: each covers 172 integrated sequences, 202 fault cases and the existing selector/register matrix. |
| `make tx-admission-check` | 11,156 checks, zero failures in each normal and ASan/UBSan run. |
| `make rx-ownership-check` | 1,123 scenarios / 331,474 checks per normal/sanitized run; wait and FLEA/LINK ISR controls also PASS. |
| `make dma-check` | PASS normal/sanitized stop and descriptor checks, including 582 FLEA reset/DDR/start/stop scenarios and nested stop holds through close/suspend. |
| `make command-pm-check` | 84 groups PASS in normal and ASan/UBSan builds, including actual context retirement across success and retained failure exits. |
| `make device-lifetime-check` | 72 scenarios and 221 existing access checks PASS in normal and ASan/UBSan builds; failed terminal proof retains quarantine, complete proof releases it. |
| `make -C driver/linux -f Makefile.in W=1 -j2` | PASS against 7.0.0-38-generic headers with the existing `-Werror` policy; not loaded or installed. |

After combining this change with #690's input-bit controls, the affected
`make tx-admission-check` was rerun: **11,548 checks, zero failures** in each
normal and ASan/UBSan run. The standalone counts above retain their own scope.

Initial test failures are preserved: an omitted extraction dependency, a test
logging macro that discarded an actual helper argument, an IRQ-count assertion
that ignored earlier setup, and old synthetic-asleep fixtures expecting normal
cleanup success. The final tests explicitly require refusal/retention for those
states. An intermediate automatic terminal-cleanup fallback was rejected in
review because it could hide unexpected faults; the final ordinary `drain()`
keeps its original success requirement. These fixture corrections do not
weaken the driver guard or supply native evidence.

### Existing diagnostic patch stack

The [first integration CI](https://github.com/ahnhy1324/crystalhd/actions/runs/45747076915)
also exposed patch-context conflicts in `fw-staging-check`, which the initial
affected-check selection missed. Four existing SCL/MFD diagnostic patches now
route their 46 post-admission failure exits through the common cleanup release.
Independent comparison of the old and refreshed applied source confirms that
their diagnostic conditions and ordering are preserved, and that the actual
PM admission helpers remain unchanged.

The temporary source copier includes the new cleanup extractor. A final
compatibility patch supplies an explicitly modelled admission/hold boundary
for the diagnostic firmware-download fixture and checks balance on every
return from its actual extracted stop function. The production PM state
decisions remain covered by the actual-helper suites above. The existing full
firmware-download, device-lifetime and probe matrix remains in
`make fw-staging-check` and the current-base CI gate.

The full staged matrix passed normal and ASan/UBSan execution: 195 download
groups, 72 lifetime scenarios in each default/research build, 221 access checks
and 596,379 probe checks, plus the existing CLI/UAPI controls. Review then found
one existing fixture initialization placed in `pci_clear_master` instead of
`reset`; its original location was restored. The affected default/research
lifetime and access suites passed again in both build modes. The other 11
generated targets are identical to the completed full run; that run is reused
for them, not claimed as a new execution of the final complete matrix.

## Still required by #689

An isolated opt-in mechanism and matched plain control must precede native
automatic transitions. Thermal comparison, repeated physical transitions,
bounded playback/endurance, recovery and the final enablement decision remain
open. The earlier single 180-frame cycle and roughly 41 microseconds asleep
remain their original bounded observation, not qualification of this change.
